messages.subject: Error with MSProcessedImagingExperiment
parts:
Hello all,

I generated imzML file from HDI (Waters software) and imported to R. I worked following CardinalWorkflows. When I tried to do peak alignment I got this Error. 

> data.peaklist <- peakAlign(data.peaklist, ref = data.norm, method = "diff",units = "ppm", diff.max = 200)
Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  : 
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘peakAlign’ for signature ‘"MSProcessedImagingExperiment", "MSProcessedImagingExperiment"’

Could you please help me? Thanks!

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Error with MSProcessedImagingExperiment
parts:
I apologize for the confusion. The CardinalWorkflows vignettes haven't been updated to reflect the new defaults and changes in Cardinal 2.2 yet.

Using another imaging dataset as a reference is not supported with the new methods, because it is somewhat ambiguous and not totally obvious that it should calculate and use the mean spectrum of that dataset; in addition, the new pre-processing functions use "delayed" execution (see the Cardinal-2-guide vignette section on pre-processing here), which means they must store their arguments, which could be problematic when using another (potentially very large) imaging dataset as a reference.

The current way to do what that line of code is attempting to do, would be:

data.peaklist <- peakAlign(data.peaklist, tolerance=200, units="ppm") %>% process()

which will use the means of the detected peaks as the reference.

If you want to follow along with CardinalWorkflows exactly, then you should import your dataset as an "MSImageSet":

data <-readMSIData("file.imzML", as="MSImageSet")

The old workflows using "MSImageSet" will continue to be supported for some time, but the old data structures and methods are not as capable of dealing with high-resolution data as the new "MSImagingExperiment" is.

We are currently working to update the CardinalWorkflows vignettes, but it will take some time. Sorry for the confusion in the meantime.

-Kylie
